title: Burst smoothing & backpressure credits for composite embedding + rerank pipelines
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem summary:

High-volume customers exhibit bursty, fanout-heavy patterns on non-chat embedding endpoints that cascade into reranker and structured toolcall stages. Our current per-request ratecap and immediate throttle semantics cause: (1) partial pipeline executions that still incur charges for prefetched embeddings or partially executed toolcalls, (2) sudden refunds that are difficult to reconcile, and (3) customer-visible billing noise and support tickets.

This ticket proposes a ratecap smoothing + backpressure-credit mechanism targeted at composite pipelines (embedding -> rerank -> toolcall) to: reduce billing churn, ensure fair quota enforcement during bursts, and make downstream attribution deterministic for reconciliation jobs. The goal is to produce measurable reduction in overcharging incidents and lower variance in hourly invoice line-items while preserving latency SLOs for steady-state traffic.
acceptance_criteria: New smoothing + credit bank implementation deployed to canary: no >0.5% increase in p95 latency for non-burst traffic
Billing reconciliation job shows <0.1% net discrepancy compared to ground truth ledger on 24h canary data
Charge visibility: per-request ledger entries include stage tags (embed|rerank|toolcall) and credit adjustments
Graceful fallbacks: when credit bank depleted, pipeline applies prioritized degradation (reranker sampling -> reduce rerank candidates -> skip optional toolcalls) rather than hard cancel
Instrumentation: Console exposes new metric set (credit_balance, smoothed_rate, deferred_executions) and alert thresholds

comments: 2026-01-16 - Asha Patel: Kickoff doc linked below. Initial notes: prefer a soft smoothing window (500ms - 2s) tuned per-customer; avoid global defaults that penalize low-latency apps.
2026-01-22 - Jordan Kim: Implemented prototype of credit bank in local dev. Observed that speculative prefetch costs can be amortized by weighting credits by stage and chance-of-execution.

2026-02-05 - PR feedback (Mina Park): Need deterministic checkpoint points to avoid double-charging when a request is retried after transient failure; propose checkpoint after embedding write and before rerank start.
2026-02-11 - Finance (L. Gomez): Acceptable drift target for canary is 0.1% discrepancy; anything above triggers rollback and detailed audit.
2026-02-26 - SRE (K. Zhou): Canary rollout plan updated: ramp 1% -> 5% -> 20% across 48h windows with automated rollback on billing-diff or error-rate spikes.

2026-03-08 - Jordan Kim: First canary run (5%) completed. Metrics: credit_balance stabilized after initial burst; p95 latency +0.24% overall. Reconciliation job shows 0.07% net discrepancy (within target). Preparing PR for runtime changes.
2026-03-10 - Review (Finance + Legal): Requested clearer customer messaging about temporary credits and refund windows (24h) and audit trail for disputes.
2026-03-12 - Jordan Kim: Addressed review comments; opened GH PR and Confluence runbook. Moving to In Review for runtime and metering teams.
metrics: deferred_executions_ratio: monitor increase <= 5% for steady workloads
customer_support_churn: measured weekly tickets related to billing (goal: -60% after rollout)
decision_log: 2026-01-20 - Chosen algorithm: leaky-bucket smoothing + per-tenant credit bank. Rationale: provides predictable smoothing for bursts while keeping accounting simple for reconciliation.
2026-02-07 - Checkpointing decision: persist soft-checkpoints (embed_done, rerank_started, toolcall_enqueued) with idempotency tokens to prevent double charges on retries.
2026-02-18 - Degradation policy: prefer quality-reduction (rerank candidate pruning) over cancellation to reduce customer-visible errors; documented in runbook.
2026-03-09 - Billing visibility: will surface credit adjustments as separate line items in Console for 30 days to aid dispute resolution.
